reader.requirement: At --std 85 FUNCTION NUMVAL-C must return the numeric value argument-1 represents in either AR1 format, ignoring the currency string cs (argument-2, any nonnumeric literal or alphanumeric item of one or more characters, else the program's currency symbol) and the commas before the decimal point, with DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA reversing comma and point.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehaviors.IsActive(NumvalCCurrencyContentRules, year): at 85 argument-2's content is not screened (no digit/*/+/-/,/./CR/DB ban) and CurrencyContentUnrestricted is set; also the ANYCASE and LOCALE keywords are COBOL-2002 constructs refused at 85
passes contentUnrestricted: true to NumvalCDec when the binder set CurrencyContentUnrestricted (the 85 arm)

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: a currency string containing '.', ',', digits or the letters CR/DB ("Fr.", "CRC") is admitted and scanned as written at 85 (§1989:A.2.30.3 AR1/AR4 constrain only its class) and refused at 2023 with COBOL1627 (§2023:15.68.3 r2); ANYCASE and LOCALE are refused at 85.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f38_05 covers the default currency symbol with a few amounts; multi-character argument-2 data items, trailing CR/DB, the 18-digit value, reference modification and ODO arguments, CURRENCY SIGN plus DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, and the 1985-only currency strings are covered by these probes (pb5161_numval_c_currency_content_85 also witnesses the last).

probes.expected: the represented values with cs and commas ignored

probes.printed: D2=-1234567,5 ("F1.234.567,5 CR" under CURRENCY SIGN IS "F" DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA) D4=3,25 ("F 3,25")
probes.expected: §1989:A.2.30.3 AR2 and AR5: reversed separators, the program currency symbol as cs

probes.printed: --std 85: E1=12345.67 ("Fr.12,345.67" "Fr.") E2=-8.5 (" Fr. 8.5 CR" with CS="Fr.") E3=-100 ("CRC 100 CR" with CS2="CRC") E4=-1000.5 ("- CRC1,000.5" "CRC"); --std 2023: COBOL1627 on the two literal currency strings
probes.expected: 85 admits any one-or-more-character cs and returns the value; 2023 refuses those literals

probes.printed: COBOL0900: the ANYCASE keyword of NUMVAL-C requires COBOL-2002; r2.cob: COBOL0900 for LOCALE

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.30.4 RV1  (2.30.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV1

reader.notes: The value comes from the same exact NvScan parse as NUMVAL, with cs and grouping commas skipped. The only edition arm, NumvalCCurrencyContentRules, is the right one at 85: a currency string the 2002+ text bans is admitted and the value is still returned correctly, including a cs containing '.' or the letters CR.

refuter.evidence: q4numval.cob at --std 85: NUMVAL-C("1,2,3") -> 123 (one-digit groups); ("12,34.5") -> 1234.5; ("USD  12" CS) with CS PIC X(5) 'USD' (trailing spaces in cs) -> 12; (" $ 7.25" CS2) with cs ' $ ' -> 7.25; ("+$.5") -> 0.5; ("$9 CR ") -> -9; ("-1,000") without cs -> -1000; ("$1,000.") -> 1000; ("XX5" "XX") -> 5. The reader's p5cs85 already covers the 1985-only currency strings and r1/r2 the 2002 keywords. q8nved.cob: a numeric-edited argument-1 refused COBOL1627 (argument rule, category reading as for NUMVAL). cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.30.4 RV1  (2.30.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV1'.
